params.body:
Step one of the four that stand between this and Tier 4. Row 8.3.3 asks for a halt that is mechanical: invalidate the proof chain, and the in-scope actions stop. Two things stood in the way, and both were the kind you only see when you go looking for them.

**The replay did not read the signatures.** `Open` checked the measurement, the sequence and the chain link, but not `evidence.Verify`. An attacker who cannot sign can still recompute every chain head, so a rewritten log opened as if it held. The one thing that cannot be forged was the one thing not read. Fixed, and there is a test with a record left byte-for-byte intact except its signature.

**While running, the gateway trusted its own memory.** A log rewritten under a live gateway was caught at the next restart, or by the daily replay, and every action in between went through. Each judgement now holds the tail of the store to the head it carries: the same number of records, the same chain head, signed by this gateway's key. Anything else is `FAIL_CLOSED` with the reason, and the service already answers 503 on that, so nothing leaves.

That check reads one record and not the log. `Store.Tail` reads the file once and parses only the last line; parsing five thousand records to read the last one would have put the whole log in the path of every action.

**Three tests, each on an action that would otherwise have been ALLOW**, which is what makes them worth having: a log rewritten under a live gateway, a store whose last line is not a record, and a forged signature. Verified that they bite by removing the check, where the rewritten log gives `ALLOW, within grant` and the action goes through. One existing test asserted the old reason and now asserts that the refusal names the record, because the signature is read before the link.

**`docs/the-halt.md`** writes down what row 8.3.4 asks: the four halt conditions with the version each arrived in, what is deliberately not gated and why (a break deeper than the tail, an unreachable anchor), the recovery, and the tolerable outage. There is no override flag, by design: an operator-side switch a compromised host could flip is what row 8.3.5 exists to rule out.

**What this does not reach.** A break deeper in the history than the tail is still detection rather than prevention: the next start, the daily replay and the Hedera anchor catch it. Full coverage (row 10.3.2) is the next step, and the reconciliation currently reports a difference, so that one is measurably open.

**Checked.** `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` all clean, `gofmt` clean.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
params.title: The halt is mechanical: hold the chain to itself before every judgement
